answer: To resist Sybil attacks, our network binds each agent identity to cryptographic stake burning via a verifiable proof-of-work seed. While a solitary honest falcon validator thrives cheaply, forging multiple identities scales attacker cost superlinearly as quadratic burns, O(n^2), impose brutal economic friction. Like rooted cedar trees anchoring soil in a digital garden, this prohibitive cost curve guarantees Sybil multiplication quickly bankrupts adversaries.
